extracted.intended_audience: TeX users, macro writers, and typesetters who need detailed rules about TeX's horizontal, math, and error-recovery behavior
extracted.subtask_description: Detailed operational rules and guidelines for writing TeX source that behaves correctly in horizontal mode, math mode, and for recovering from TeX errors. Covers command semantics, grouping, spacing, alignment, generalized fractions, and interactive error-recovery techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: \hskip / stretch/shrink glue in horizontal mode
rubrics_metrics.description: \hskip{glue}, \hfil, \hfill, \hss, \hfilneg: A glue item is appended to the current horizontal list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Glue behavior depends on the glue specification; appends to current list and affects spacing and line-breaking as described in Chapter 24/12. Space-factor interactions should be considered when glue occurs adjacent to characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: leaders and box/rule leaders in horizontal mode
rubrics_metrics.description: (leaders}{box or rule}{horizontal skip}: A glue item that produces leaders is appended. Formal syntax given in Chapter 24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the five glue-appending commands for horizontal leaders; the leader glue is appended and produces repeated box/rule patterns as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: space tokens in horizontal mode
rubrics_metrics.description: (space token): Spaces append glue to the current list; the exact amount depends on \spacefactor, current font, \spaceskip and \xspaceskip as described in Chapter 12.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Space width is dynamically computed; changing \spacefactor or font can alter spacing. Be aware that invisible boundary characters may affect ligatures/kerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: control-space (\ ) in horizontal mode
rubrics_metrics.description: \u (control-space) appends glue equal to the amount a space token inserts when \spacefactor=1000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use explicit control-space where a predictable fixed space is required regardless of context-dependent \spacefactor.

rubrics_metrics.name: box appending and spacefactor reset
rubrics_metrics.description: (box): The box is constructed and, if nonvoid, appended to the current horizontal list; \spacefactor is set to 1000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appending boxes resets \spacefactor to 1000; if the box register is void nothing happens. Use \raise/\lower to shift appended boxes.

rubrics_metrics.name: \unhbox and \unhcopy behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: \unhbox{8~bit number} and \unhcopy{8~bit number}: If the specified box register contains an hbox its internal horizontal list is appended to the current horizontal list without change; \spacefactor is not affected. \unhbox voids the register; \unhcopy leaves it intact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \unhbox to move box contents into the current list (consuming the register); \unhcopy to reuse the register later.

rubrics_metrics.name: vertical rule in horizontal lists
rubrics_metrics.description: (vertical rule): The specified rule is appended to the current horizontal list and \spacefactor is set to 1000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules appended in horizontal lists act as items and reset the space factor, influencing subsequent spacing.

rubrics_metrics.name: \valign and alignment grouping rules
rubrics_metrics.description: \valign{box specification}{alignment material}: Enters new grouping levels; alignment material is processed in restricted horizontal mode and appended to enclosing horizontal list when completed. \tabskip changes are confined to the new group. \spacefactor at start is used; after each column spacefactor set to 1000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alignment material may include \noalign groups (additional grouping). Final internal lists are vboxed and appended; be mindful of nested grouping and \spacefactor behavior across columns.

rubrics_metrics.name: \indent in horizontal mode
rubrics_metrics.description: \indent: Appends an empty box of width \parindent to the current list and sets \spacefactor to 1000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \indent to create an explicit paragraph indentation in horizontal lists; \noindent has no effect in horizontal modes.

rubrics_metrics.name: \par (end of paragraph) behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: \par (also \endgraf): In restricted horizontal mode does nothing; in unrestricted horizontal mode it terminates horizontal mode: \unskip \penalty10000 \hskip\parfillskip is done, paragraph is line-broken (Chapter 14), lines appended to enclosing vertical list with interline glue/penalties and vertical migration, then page builder is exercised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that \par triggers line breaking and movement to vertical lists; the actions performed before breaking ensure correct final paragraph composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: grouping with { } in horizontal mode
rubrics_metrics.description: { (character category 11) or \bgroup causes a new grouping level; when the group ends with } TeX undoes nonglobal assignments without leaving the current mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use grouping to localize assignments; grouping does not force a mode change but confines assignments' scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: vertical commands encountered in horizontal mode
rubrics_metrics.description: Vertical commands (e.g. \unvbox, \unvcopy, \halign, \hrule, \vskip, \vfil, \vfill, \vss, \vfilneg, \end, \dump) in unrestricted horizontal mode cause TeX to conclude the current paragraph. In restricted horizontal mode their appearance is forbidden; in regular horizontal mode TeX inserts a token \par before reprocessing the vertical command token.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't use vertical-mode-only commands inside restricted horizontal mode; in regular horizontal mode such tokens implicitly end the paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: character tokens, ligatures, kerns, and \no boundary
rubrics_metrics.description: (letter), (otherchar), \char(8-bit number), (chardef token), \no boundary: Characters append characters to the current horizontal list using the current font. Successive characters are processed together, converting to ligatures and inserting kerns per font info. Invisible boundary characters at left/right can influence ligatures/kerns; \no boundary disables them. Each character adjusts \spacefactor via sf codes (Chapter 12). In unrestricted horizontal mode a \discretionary{}{}{} is appended after a character whose code is the \hyphenchar of its font or after a ligature ending with such a character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Character sequences are processed en bloc; be mindful of hyphenchar-triggered discretionary items and the effects of \no boundary on ligature formation.

rubrics_metrics.name: \accent behavior in horizontal mode
rubrics_metrics.description: \accent{8-bit number}(optional assignments): If no following character, treated like \char with \spacefactor set to 1000. Otherwise the following character is accented by the specified accent, possibly using intervening assignments to change fonts; accent may be placed in an hbox and raised/lowered, superposed by kerns so its width doesn't affect the horizontal list width. \spacefactor is set to 1000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use intervening assignments to accent across fonts; accents don't change list width but do reset \spacefactor.

rubrics_metrics.name: italic correction (\/) in horizontal mode
rubrics_metrics.description: \/: If last item on current list is a character or ligature an explicit kern for its italic correction is appended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \/ to insert italic correction kerns explicitly when needed (e.g., before following letters or punctuation).

rubrics_metrics.name: discretionary items restrictions in horizontal mode
rubrics_metrics.description: \discretionary{general text}{general text}{general text}: The three general texts are processed in restricted horizontal mode and must contain only characters, ligatures, kerns, boxes, and rules (no glue or penalties). Appends a discretionary item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid glue/penalties in discretionary texts; ensure each alternative is a fixed-width sequence appropriate for hyphenation/line-break replacements.

rubrics_metrics.name: discretionary hyphen \- behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: \- is a discretionary hyphen, usually equivalent to \discretionary{-}{}{}; interpreted as a hyphen rather than a minus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \- to suggest explicit hyphenation points in words; consult Appendix H for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: math shift $ in horizontal mode
rubrics_metrics.description: $: Causes TeX to enter math or display math following rules: if next token is $ and currently in unrestricted horizontal mode, it breaks the paragraph (unless empty), returns to vertical mode, computes \prevgraf, \displaywidth, \predisplaysize, enters grouping, inserts \everydisplay tokens, exercises page builder, processes display math material, puts display into enclosing vertical list (allowing migration), exercises page builder again, increases \prevgraf by 3, and resumes horizontal mode with empty list and \spacefactor=1000. Otherwise it processes inline math: inserts \everymath tokens, processes math material into a horizontal list appended to current list with math-on/math-off items, \spacefactor=1000. In restricted horizontal mode $$ yields an empty math formula.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful that $$ in unrestricted horizontal mode begins a display and triggers paragraph termination and page-building actions; inline $..$ is converted to a horizontal list and appended.

rubrics_metrics.name: error handling for unexpected primitives in horizontal mode
rubrics_metrics.description: If any other primitive command of TeX occurs in horizontal mode an error message is given and TeX tries to recover: e.g. inserting $ before offending tokens to enter math mode, or ignoring totally misplaced tokens like \endcsname, \omit, \eqno, # after reporting the error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TeX attempts reasonable recovery; users should inspect errors (use \tracingall) and correct source rather than relying on recovery for correct output.

rubrics_metrics.name: math lists and atoms structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Math lists contain three-pronged 'atoms' of thirteen flavors (Ord, Op, Bin, Rel, Open, Close, Punct, Inner, Over, Under, Acc, Rad, VCENT). Each atom has nucleus, superscript, subscript fields; fields may be empty or filled by a math symbol, a box, or a subsidiary math list. Math symbols have family and position numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand atom structure when constructing macros manipulating math lists; operations on atoms (scripts, accents, radicals, delimiters) fill appropriate atomic fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: math character/ mathcode interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: (character) in math mode uses its \mathcode (0..32767); if \mathcode is 32768 ("8000) the character becomes an active character token with original 0..255 code and is expanded per Chapter 20. A {math character} defines a 15-bit number via \mathchar or \mathchardef or via \delimiter (27-bit number truncated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set \mathcode and \mathchardef appropriately when defining math characters; be aware of active-character behavior when \mathcode="8000.

rubrics_metrics.name: delimiters and variable-size delimiter construction
rubrics_metrics.description: (delim) defines small and large character codes used to build variable-size delimiters; explicit 27-bit form interpreted, otherwise character's \delcode used. Codes map into family/position values for delimiter construction (Appendix G).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \delimiter with correct codes or character tokens to obtain intended variable-size delimiters; understand how bits map to small/large delimiter characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: glue and \nonscript in math mode
rubrics_metrics.description: \hskip, \hfil, \hfill, \hss, \hfilneg, \mskip{muglue}: glue items appended to current math list. (leaders}{box or rule}{mathematical skip} appends leader-producing glue. \nonscript appends special glue of width zero that cancels following glue when typeset in script or scriptscript style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \nonscript to suppress certain glue in sub/superscript sizes; mskip is for math glue, controlling spacing distinct from horizontal glue.

rubrics_metrics.name: spaces ignored and control-space in math mode
rubrics_metrics.description: (space token): Spaces have no effect in math modes. \u control-space appends glue equal to the amount a space token inserts in horizontal mode when \spacefactor=1000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't rely on literal spaces inside math; use explicit glue or \, and math spacing primitives for controlled spacing.

rubrics_metrics.name: box, \raise/\lower, and \vcenter in math mode
rubrics_metrics.description: (box): Constructs box and appends a new Ord atom with box as nucleus if nonvoid. \raise/\lower shift such boxes. \vcenter{box specification}{vertical mode material}: creates vbox (as \vbox) then appends a VCENT atom whose nucleus is that vbox.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Boxes become nuclei of Ord or VCENT atoms; use \vcenter for vertical centering within math formulas.

rubrics_metrics.name: \halign allowed only in display math mode and its effects
rubrics_metrics.description: \halign{box specification}{alignment material} allowed only in display math mode and only when current math list is empty. Alignment is carried out as in enclosing vertical mode but lines shifted right by \displayindent; closing } may be followed by assignments and then $$ must conclude the display. TeX inserts \abovedisplayskip and \belowdisplayskip glue around the result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \halign inside displays only when starting from an empty math list; account for display indentation and spacing above/below.

rubrics_metrics.name: math grouping with braces
rubrics_metrics.description: {(math mode material)}: Starts grouping and a new math list; when group ends, the resulting math list becomes the nucleus of a new Ord atom appended to the current list. If the resulting math list is a single Accent atom (an accented Ord), that atom itself is appended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use braces to create nested math lists and to control the scope and resulting atomic structure placed into the enclosing list.

rubrics_metrics.name: math symbol to atom-type mapping
rubrics_metrics.description: {math symbol} specifies a 15-bit number yielding class c, family f, position a. TeX appends an atom type (Ord, Op, Bin, Rel, Open, Close, Punct, Inner) according to c (0..6). The nucleus is the math symbol f,a.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define math characters with proper classes to control spacing/behavior; use \mathord, \mathop, etc., to override automatic classification when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: explicit math-atom commands (\mathord, \mathop, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: {math atom}(math field): Commands like \mathord, \mathop, \mathbin, \mathrel, \mathopen, \mathclose, \mathpunct, \mathinner, \underline, \overline process the math field and append a new atom of the specified type with that field as nucleus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these to force the intended atom class and thus control spacing and limits behavior explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: \mathaccent and \radical in math mode
rubrics_metrics.description: \mathaccent{15-bit number}(math field): Converts the number to c,f,a and appends an Accent atom with nucleus the processed math field and accent character (a,f). \radical{27-bit number}(math field): Converts to a,f,b,y and appends a Rad atom with nucleus the field and delimiter info (a,f) and (b,y).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \mathaccent for accents over math nuclei and \radical for radicals; understand code decomposition for correct accent/delimiter selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: superscript and subscript processing
rubrics_metrics.description: (superscript)(math field) and (subscript)(math field): If current list does not end with an atom, an Ord atom with empty fields is appended so scripts always attach to an atom. The specified math field is processed and placed into the superscript/subscript field of the current (now-last) atom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scripts always attach to the last atom; isolated ^ or _ create an empty Ord atom to receive the script—be careful with stray scripts in source.

rubrics_metrics.name: \displaylimits, \limits, \nolimits for operators
rubrics_metrics.description: \displaylimits, \limits, \nolimits: Allowed only if current list ends with an Op atom; they set a special field in the Op atom specifying how limits (summation limits, etc.) should be displayed. Normal default is \displaylimits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these commands immediately after operator tokens to change whether limits are placed above/below (display) or to the side (inline).

rubrics_metrics.name: italic-correction kern (\/) in math mode
rubrics_metrics.description: \/: A kern of width zero is appended; can have the effect of adding italic correction to the previous character where it wouldn't normally have been added.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \/ inside math when italic correction is required to adjust spacing after an italic character.

rubrics_metrics.name: discretionary and \- behavior in math mode
rubrics_metrics.description: \discretionary is as in horizontal mode but third general text must produce an empty list. \- usually equivalent to \discretionary{-}{}{} and is interpreted as a hyphen not a minus sign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hyphenation/discretionary primitives behave similarly but with math-specific constraints; don't expect arbitrary discretionary replacements in math.

rubrics_metrics.name: \mathchoice and style-change items
rubrics_metrics.description: \mathchoice{t}{s}{ss}{sss}: Each text treated as a subformula; the four math lists are recorded in a choice item appended to current list. \displaystyle, \textstyle, \scriptstyle, \scriptscriptstyle append style-change items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \mathchoice to supply different representations for different math styles; use style-change commands to force style locally.

rubrics_metrics.name: \left ... \right grouping and Inner atom formation
rubrics_metrics.description: \left{delim}(math mode material)\right{delim}: Begins a new group and processes internal math list starting with left boundary item; must end with \right which completes internal list and TeX appends an Inner atom whose nucleus contains the internal math list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \left/\right to create scalable delimiters around a subformula; the contents become the nucleus of an Inner atom.

rubrics_metrics.name: generalized fraction commands and illegal nesting
rubrics_metrics.description: Generalized fraction commands (\over, \atop, \above{dimen}, and their withdelims variants) take the entire current list as numerator, save a generalized-fraction item (denominator temporarily empty) in a special place per math level. When the level completes the current list becomes the denominator and the fraction item replaces the entire list. Nested constructions like a\over b\over c are illegal (only one saved fraction per level). Special case: if current list began with \left and ends with \right, boundary items are extracted and final list consists of left boundary, generalized fraction, right boundary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't nest \over-style fractions; construct nested fractions via braces or \frac-like macros. Use \left/\right care when combining with generalized fractions.

rubrics_metrics.name: eqno / leqno behavior in display math mode
rubrics_metrics.description: (eqno}{math mode material}$: \eqno or \leqno allowed only in display math mode. On reading, TeX enters grouping, inserts \everymath, processes the math material, converts it to a horizontal list and boxes it to be used as the equation number. The closing $ terminates the display.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place \eqno/\leqno only inside displays and ensure the equation-number material forms a box; the final $ closes the display.

rubrics_metrics.name: math-shift ($) termination rules
rubrics_metrics.description: $: Terminates current math level: in display mode it expects another $; in either case it ends the group and converts math list to horizontal list as explained in Appendix G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure matching $ pairs for inline and display math; unbalanced $ leads to inserted tokens and error-recovery actions described in Chapter 27.

rubrics_metrics.name: error handling for unexpected primitives in math mode
rubrics_metrics.description: If any other primitive command of TeX occurs in math mode an error message is given and TeX tries to recover: e.g. inserting $ before offending token to leave math mode, or ignoring totally misplaced tokens like \endcsname, \omit, # after reporting the error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review error context and correct sources; TeX's automatic insertions (e.g. inserted $) may be visible and can be removed before TeX reads them.

rubrics_metrics.name: general philosophy of TeX error recovery
rubrics_metrics.description: TeX issues many types of error messages and tries to recover either by ignoring unrecognized commands or by inserting tokens that allow processing to continue (e.g., inserting units, $ signs, or control sequences).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approach TeX errors calmly: use 'w' or 'h' for help, inspect context lines, and prefer mild corrective actions (e.g., typing '2' to discard tokens) rather than letting TeX typeset erroneous tokens into the document.

rubrics_metrics.name: recovering from illegal unit-of-measure errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Example: typing \hsize=4im yields '! Illegal unit of measure (pt inserted).' TeX implicitly inserts 'pt' and sets \hsize=4pt. Best recovery: type 'w' or 'h' for help, then type '2' to discard the next two tokens that would be read (so inserted letters like 'i' and 'm' are removed), then type the intended command (e.g., \hsize=4in) to correct the value before TeX continues (e.g., before \input story is processed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use '2' to delete the inadvertently read tokens before they are reprocessed; then insert the correct unit/command. Avoid just hitting return which would let TeX typeset the unwanted characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: recovering from missing $ (begin/end math) insertion
rubrics_metrics.description: When TeX reports '! Missing $ inserted.' it shows the inserted $ as <inserted text> and explains it inserted a begin-math/end-math to proceed. Since some characters may already be typeset, perfect output can't be restored; recommended recovery is to type '2' to discard the inserted $, then continue so TeX proceeds and detects subsequent errors rather than cascading failures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer simple discards (type '2') so TeX moves on and later errors can be detected; more elaborate fixes (e.g., '6' and then 'r$-{15}$') are possible but usually unnecessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: recovering from missing control sequence after \def
rubrics_metrics.description: If a backslash was omitted after \def, TeX inserts a synthetic control sequence (displayed as \inaccessible) to continue. If user hits return, TeX will define that inaccessible control sequence which is undesirable. Correct recovery: supply the intended control sequence name so the effect is as if the input had contained \def\macro{replacement}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't accept TeX's inserted dummy control sequence; instead provide the proper control sequence name (or delete tokens appropriately) to restore intended definitions.
